A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Orthus. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original Orthus benchmark results, training and embedding ablations, image reconstruction measurements, and qualitative multimodal generation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds quantitative image-editing comparisons and qualitative editing experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the causal transformer, differentiable vision embedding, language and diffusion heads, combined training objective, and modality-switching inference. Image editing applies the existing post-training procedure without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds Instruct-Pix2Pix training and evaluation, extending coverage to instruction-based image editing, real-image transfer and example-conditioned editing. Standard visual benchmarks and StoryStream remain. The text-prompted, zero-shot Orthus-base interleaving demonstrations from v1 Figure 4 are omitted.

E2.justification: v2 adds PnP, SDEdit and InstructPix2Pix editing comparisons. Existing benchmark tables add Emu3-Chat and Emu3-Gen but remove mPLUG-Owl2, IDEFICS-9B, LlamaGen, PixArt-alpha and the original Chameleon generation row. The appendix-only LDM comparison also disappears. Post-trained Chameleon remains.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a distinct editing protocol: fine-tuning Orthus-base on 400k Instruct-Pix2Pix training examples, evaluating its test set with CLIP-T/I/D similarities, and testing prompts containing editing examples instead of explicit instructions. These are added experimental settings; newly documented budgets and reconstruction holdout details do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: The separate-versus-unified training, embedding-choice, MSE-loss and reconstruction analyses remain unchanged. v2 adds limited qualitative tests of real-image generalization, in-context editing and preservation of unedited regions in Figures 3 and 8, while removing two zero-shot Orthus-base generation demonstrations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its empirical results. v2's additional training-step counts are not repeated-run information.

E6.justification: Retained Orthus scores remain unchanged, including GenEval 0.58, HPSv2 28.2 and MME-P 1265.8. v2 adds editing CLIP-T/I/D scores of 0.238/0.87/0.049, versus InstructPix2Pix's 0.233/0.88/0.045, plus Emu3 results and editing examples. It removes the six GenEval category breakdowns, detailed HPSv2 category results, deleted comparator rows and zero-shot interleaving examples.

T1.justification: The VQ mapping, embedding equations, diffusion objective and combined autoregressive/diffusion objective are unchanged. Neither the main text nor appendices introduce or revise formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: v2's introduction newly claims superiority over InstructPix2Pix and in-context learning capabilities for unseen tasks. The central contributions—unified autoregressive modeling of continuous images and discrete text, inexpensive construction, and improved visual benchmark performance—remain intact; interleaved generation was already central to v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets editing examples as evidence of generalization, in-context learning and potential as a foundation multimodal model; Figure 8 claims better preservation of unedited regions. It removes v1's explanations of the SD3 gap and Transfusion comparison through captioning and training-data advantages. Existing ablation interpretations and future scaling directions remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository link. Appendix B specifies selection of the first 10k training images, batch sizes 32/16 and 15,000/35,000 steps for base/instruction training. Appendix A adds decoder learning rate, batch size, training steps and explicit training/evaluation separation. These are new disclosures, not established reruns. Conversely, v1's 1:1 data-mixing ratio and cosine-scheduler disclosure are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds editing-method and CLIP-evaluation references and contrasts its interleaved capabilities with Janus and JanusFlow. It removes the HART discussion, DreamLLM citation and several benchmark references. The principal positioning relative to MAR, Chameleon, Show-o and Transfusion remains; Emu3 was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is reorganized to lead with interleaved tasks, combine visual understanding and generation, and condense benchmark descriptions. The abstract, introduction and post-training explanation are revised, and appendices are reorganized around new training details. An Impact Statement is added, citations switch to author-year format, and Zhihong Liu joins the author list.

P2.justification: v2 compresses the full-width generation breakdown into an overall-score table, adds editing and training tables, and removes v1's detailed HPSv2 table. It replaces the zero-shot half of v1 Figure 4 with editing panels while retaining the storybook examples, and adds Figure 8. Headers, captions and appendix layout change substantially; retained galleries and chat examples are relocated.

improvement.justification: The editing comparison in v2 Table 1 provides quantitative support for an additional mixed-modality application, while Appendices A–B improve reproducibility through training budgets and explicit holdout disclosure. These provide a limited net gain. Benefits are tempered by removal of diagnostic GenEval/HPSv2 breakdowns and some training settings; the new generalization and in-context claims still rest on a few qualitative examples.
